the rail groups rounds under their parent (children indented, chronological within the thread, 'Round N' chip; an orphan child whose parent is outside the capped view stays visible with its round number)

p0_2_time_expectation.finding: 'runs take minutes; you can leave and come back' lived in the 12.5px keyboard-hint grey — product-critical duration information whispered in a footer; a first-time user watches a blank conversation with no sense of progress (the audit's BLOCKER 3)
the_fix: the landing carries the duration at FULL visual weight (hero-note, 14px, ink-soft, its own block): 'A discovery run takes minutes, not seconds. … you can leave this page and come back' — minutes as an honest CLASS, never a precise promise (the same discipline as the elapsed-time line)
the keyboard hint returns to being a keyboard hint
the RUNNING conversation's opening note states the duration class + the resume guarantee

the live sentence carries the run's POSITION: stageProgressSuffix (productEvents.ts) — distinct COMPLETED stages + the active one, from recorded events only. 'Stage 3 of 13' was REFUSED on Art. XXV/VI grounds: the pipeline's length varies by run and inventing a denominator would fabricate an expectation. The suffix reads '· step N' — position only, no total, no stage names

p0_3_first_use_orientation.finding: a new user cannot answer 'what does this produce?' within 20 seconds of landing (the audit's BLOCKER 5 / Part §A)
the_fix: the EXAMPLE RESULT card (expect-card) under the suggestions: what a finished discovery looks like — evidence found, competing candidates with kill conditions, the adversarial challenge, the engineering + 3D model, the decisive experiment, the downloadable package
labeled 'An illustrative example — every real result states its own evidence and its own limits, never more' (never a fake record; the card mirrors the REAL result vocabulary)
the duration note (P0-2) completes the 20-second answer: how long + what you receive + the suggestion chips' what-kind-of-problem

p0_4_wcag_aa_accent.finding: --accent #c15f3c ≈ 4.2:1 on white / 4.0:1 on paper at 11-13px in .card .kicker, .arg .step .k, .ic-title, .rail-inv-id, .linklike, hover text, .chip.on on its tint — a measurable AA failure (the audit's BLOCKER 4)
the_fix: THREE tokens, measured in tests (not asserted by eye): --accent #c15f3c (borders/fills/large type, unchanged), --accent-text #a34d2e (5.7:1 white / 5.5:1 paper / 5.0:1 paper-2), --accent-deep #8f4220 (5.3:1 on the accent-soft tint — .chip.on)
every small-text accent context switched to the AA token (kicker, step keys, ic-title, rail-inv-id, linklike, chip on/hover, all hover-text states); borders/backgrounds stay --accent
--warn darkened #a86a2f → #96601f (4.4:1 → 5.3:1 on white; 4.8:1 on its pill tint) — the same class of measurable failure, fixed in the same pass
the ratios are COMPUTED in tests/adversarial_r464.test.mjs (the luminance formula in the test) — the acceptance is arithmetic, not opinion
